subject: Automotive & EVs
title: How eVTOLs Work
description: Learn How eVTOLs Work in one minute.

hook.text: An eVTOL uses multiple electric rotors to lift off vertically—no runway, no long taxiway, no jet fuel.

buildup.text: Most designs use between 6 and 18 rotors for redundancy—if one fails, the others keep flying safely.

discovery.text: Once airborne, some designs tilt their rotors or wings forward to fly like an airplane for efficiency.

twist.text: Current battery limits restrict range to about 60 to 100 miles—enough for city hops, not cross-country trips.

climax.text: Joby Aviation, Lilium, and Archer are racing to be the first to carry paying passengers by 2025.

punchline.text: Electric helicopters that fly like planes could be the next urban transit.

quiz.question: Why do eVTOLs use multiple rotors?
options: For redundancy and safety if one rotor fails
